questions.question: What is the main purpose of the long parallel mid-body on a bulk carrier?
questions.explanation: The long parallel mid-body provides maximum internal volume for cargo holds, increasing cargo capacity.

questions.question: What is the typical block coefficient (Cb) of a bulk carrier?
questions.explanation: Bulk carriers have a full-form hull with a block coefficient typically between 0.70 and 0.80.

questions.question: Why do bulk carriers usually have a high ballast capacity?
options: To maintain an efficient draft and propeller immersion when unloaded
To reduce the size of the cargo holds
questions.explanation: Large ballast tanks help maintain proper draft, trim and propeller immersion during ballast voyages.

questions.question: Which stern design is commonly used on modern bulk carriers?
questions.explanation: Modern bulk carriers almost universally use a transom stern for improved hydrodynamic performance.

questions.question: Why are bulk carrier hulls longitudinally stiffened?
questions.explanation: Bulk carriers experience significant longitudinal bending loads, making longitudinal stiffening the preferred structural arrangement.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a duct keel in a double-bottom bulk carrier?
options: To provide space for pipelines and support loads during dry docking
questions.explanation: The duct keel carries pipelines and also transfers loads to keel blocks when the vessel is dry docked.

questions.question: What is the purpose of hopper tanks in bulk carrier cargo holds?
options: To improve cargo trimming and reduce cargo shifting
questions.explanation: Hopper tanks create sloped sides that help cargo flow toward the centerline, making the holds self-trimming.

questions.question: Why is the sheer strake normally thicker than the adjacent deck or side shell plating?
options: Because this area experiences high stress concentrations
questions.explanation: The deck-to-side shell connection experiences high stresses, requiring increased plate thickness.

questions.question: What is one major advantage of a double-hull bulk carrier compared to a single-hull design?
options: Improved stability and additional ballast capacity
questions.explanation: Double-hull designs provide wing ballast tanks that improve stability and increase safety.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of corrugated transverse bulkheads?
options: To eliminate the need for separate stiffeners
questions.explanation: Corrugations provide structural strength without requiring additional stiffeners, resulting in a better strength-to-weight ratio.

questions.question: What is the primary advantage of alternate hold loading?
options: It improves cargo weight distribution and minimizes cargo shifting
questions.explanation: Alternate hold loading distributes heavy cargo more evenly and keeps holds either full or empty, reducing cargo movement.

questions.question: Why are bulk carrier hatch openings made very large?
options: To allow rapid loading and unloading of bulk cargo
questions.explanation: Large hatch openings allow efficient loading and discharge using grabs, conveyors and shore equipment.
